scope: every work cited in docs/whitepaper/0*.md and 10-related-work.md: 50 keys, all of references.bib
method: Each citing sentence was compared with the cited work's full text: arXiv HTML for the 39 arXiv works, the vendor documentation page for the 8 product citations, the 1960 edition of Ashby on archive.org and the authors' PDF of Brun et al. Filieri et al. could only be checked against its abstract. Claims about Roko and the status matrix were not changed.

summary.note: All five corrections are minor. Three works shared one sentence that credited them with held-out tests and rollback, the guard Roko's own design (§5) uses. One citation pointed at the wrong Claude Code page. One product page was paraphrased beyond its text.

works.title: Cheap Verifiers, Large Blind Spots: Measuring the Reliability Cost of Cost-Saving Cascades

sentences.text: In a cascade answering math questions, the verifier passed 12% to 55% of a cheap student's wrong answers, more as the student grew; a frontier verifier cut that to about 5% but escalated 46% of hard queries, giving the saving back [@rajput2026cheap].

Its regulators act on them within a run (retry, escalation, split) and across runs (routing, task sizing), and its audits check the regulators (§5), because metrics read through a loop's own verifier can hide its decline [@rajput2026cheap].
Cheap verifiers have blind spots: on hard MATH queries a cascade's dashboard read a flat 3% error while delivered error reached 32% [@rajput2026cheap].

works.evidence: Blind-spot rate beta grows with student size, 0.12 to 0.55; a frontier verifier drives beta to ~0.05 but escalates on 46% of hard-MATH queries; the dashboard reads a flat ~3% error while true delivered error swings up to 32% (abstract, §5, §6).

sentences.text: Models fail more as tasks get longer, and small ones far sooner [@kwa2025measuring; @sinha2025illusion]; §2 gives the settings.

Size tasks for the executor, not for cohesion.** On software and research tasks timed against human experts, the task length models complete with 80% success is 4–6× shorter than at 50% [@kwa2025measuring]; on a synthetic long task, per-step errors compound [@sinha2025illusion].
Retry twice cheaply, then escalate, then split.** On the same synthetic task, models erred more once their own mistakes were in context [@sinha2025illusion].

works.evidence: Step-accuracy gains compound over a long horizon (§2.1); the self-conditioning effect: models err more once their own errors are in context (§3.2); larger models execute longer (§3.1).
